meta.title: Mumbai new domestic water connection grid-only evidence ledger
meta.disclaimer: Independent research, not official advice. Grid-only benchmark run: sources and claims only, no nodes, edges, roadblocks or journeys. Desk research, no counter visited. Limitations: the corporation publishes no guidance page for a new water connection, only two application forms in a document folder whose files were last changed on 18 September 2015; the procedure, the document lists, the step-by-step time limits and the deciding officers come from ward-level Section 4 RTI manuals of the Hydraulic Engineer's Department, whose file metadata dates them to 2015 and 2017, so they are treated as potentially outdated official material even though two different wards publish the same text; the Manual of Water Charges Rules and the Manual of Water Bye-Laws are recorded by those manuals as available from the PRO department on payment of fees rather than published, so no connection charge or deposit figure could be read; the application form was read but never filled in or submitted. Do not submit personal data through this ledger.

agencies.name: Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai, Hydraulic Engineer's Department

scenarios.label: Mumbai new domestic water connection
scenarios.summary: The individual owner of a built residential property with no connection applies to the city's water utility for a new domestic water supply, with sewer only where the same application covers it. Bulk or high-rise connections, commercial use, regularisation of unauthorised connections, name transfer on an existing account and tanker supply are excluded.

sources.title: New Water Connection - MyBMC document folder
sources.notes: Jurisdiction: Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. Agency naming as displayed on the access date: 'MyBMC - Welcome to BMC's Website'. Direct current observation of a public official interface: the route renders a document folder holding exactly two files, an application form for the slum category and one for other categories, each showing a 'Changed On' date of 18 September 2015, and no guidance text of any kind. Archive: the Wayback availability API returned no snapshot for this route on the access date; the original official URL is retained and the capture failure is recorded here as a limitation. No new capture was pushed from this run.

sources.title: Application form for new water connection for other categories
sources.notes: Jurisdiction: Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. Agency naming as displayed on the access date: the form's Marathi masthead reads 'Brihanmumbai Mahanagarpalika, Jal Abhiyanta Khate' (Hydraulic Engineer's Department). The form is currently published on the corporation's own new-connection route and is read here as an observed current official form; the folder listing gives its last change as 18 September 2015, which is recorded as a limitation on its currency. It was read only: nothing was filled in, printed or submitted. Archive: an existing Wayback snapshot was found at https://web.archive.org/web/20220307174231/https://portal.mcgm.gov.in/irj/go/km/docs/documents/NewWaterConnection/2%20Application%20form%20for%20new%20water%20connection%20for%20other%20categories.pdf (2022-03-07); no new capture was pushed from this run.

sources.title: Section 4 Manuals as per provision of RTI Act 2005 of K/West Ward - Assistant Water Work Department, Hydraulic Engineer's Department
sources.notes: Jurisdiction: Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. Agency naming as displayed on the access date: 'BRIHANMUMBAI MAHANAGARPALIKA' and 'MUNICIPAL CORPORATION OF GREATER MUMBAI, Hydraulic Engineer's Department'. Forty-four pages, published by the office of the Assistant Engineer (Water Works), K/West ward under section 4 of the RTI Act. It carries no visible issue date; the PDF metadata records a creation date of 2017-03-02, so claims from it are graded C as potentially outdated official material. Its provenance is one ward, which is recorded as a limitation on reading it as the city-wide procedure. Archive: an existing Wayback snapshot was found at https://web.archive.org/web/20220307174203/https://portal.mcgm.gov.in/irj/go/km/docs/documents/MCGM%20Department%20List/Wards/Assistant%20Commissioner%20(KWest-Ward)/RTI%20Manuals/WaterWorksDept.pdf (2022-03-07); no new capture was pushed from this run.

sources.title: RTI 17 Manual, Assistant Engineer Water Works, D Ward
sources.notes: Jurisdiction: Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. Agency naming as displayed on the access date: 'BRIHANMUMBAI MAHANAGARPALIKA'. sources.title: Water bill payment and duplicate bill or receipt download - BMC water citizen portal
sources.notes: Jurisdiction: Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. Agency naming as displayed on the access date: 'Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC)'. The page footer displays 'Last Updated on 05/09/2026', recorded as publishedAt. Direct current observation of a public official interface. It serves an existing consumer number and is cited here only for what happens once a connection exists, not for the application route. Archive: an existing Wayback snapshot was found at https://web.archive.org/web/20260606021528/https://aquaptax.mcgm.gov.in/aqua/CitizenHome.html (2026-06-06); no new capture was pushed from this run.

claims.text: The corporation's application form for a new water connection for other categories states a scrutiny fee of Rs. 200.
claims.notes: An amount the citizen pays at the scrutiny step. It is the only figure any reviewed route states for this service.

claims.text: The ward water works RTI manual records the Manual of Water Charges Rules and the Manual of Water Bye-Laws for water connections as available with the PRO department on payment of fees, rather than as published documents.
claims.notes: Recorded because it explains why no connection charge or deposit figure could be found on any public route.

claims.text: The ward water works RTI manual states that standard application forms are available in the wards, and that the applicant fills in the form, attaches references and requisite documents, and submits the papers in the respective ward through a licensed plumber.
claims.notes: The same sentence appears verbatim in the manuals of two different wards, which is why both are cited.

claims.text: The ward water works RTI manual lists the documents for a water connection to a planned building as a no-objection certificate from the Hydraulic Engineer's Department, a copy of the plans approved by the planning authority, a copy of the IOD, amended plans or commencement certificate, a copy of the occupation certificate or building completion certificate, and a copy of any other applicable no-objection certificate.
claims.notes: The category that covers an authorised built residential property, which is this scenario's trigger.

claims.text: The ward water works RTI manual lists the documents for a water connection to a tolerable structure as a copy of the assessment bill of the structure, a copy of the ration card, a copy of the rent receipt and a no-objection certificate from the owner of the premises.
claims.notes: A second document list, for the older-structure category, alongside the planned-building one.

claims.text: The ward water works RTI manual sets out separate document requirements by connection category, covering stand-post connections for slum dwellers, connections to a tolerable structure, connections to a planned building, connections on humanitarian grounds, connections for commercial use and unmetered connections for construction purposes.
claims.notes: A rule that decides which document set and which route apply to a given property.

claims.text: The ward water works RTI manual publishes a step-by-step time limit table for granting a water connection: scrutiny of the application 15 days, letter to the party 2 days, compliance by the party with the scrutiny fee 30 days, site visit report after compliance 7 days, proposal to higher authority 15 days, recommendation by the Assistant Engineer Water Works 5 days, approval or rejection by the competent higher authority 7 days at each level, preparation of the permission form or rejection letter 7 days, signature 7 days, and issue of the permission form with the connection form 2 days.
claims.notes: The same table appears in the manuals of two different wards. It covers the sanction stage only; the manual gives the installation stage separately.

claims.text: The ward water works RTI manual gives further time limits after the permission form: compliance with the permission and connection forms within one year by the plumber or applicant, road opening permit 15 days, preparation of the meter card 10 days, physical connection of the water meter 7 days, and generation of the consumer number with updating of the meter reading card 10 days.

The ward water works RTI manual states that approval of a new or additional connection rests, depending on the powers vested in each, with the Assistant Engineer, the Executive Engineer, the Deputy Hydraulic Engineer and the Hydraulic Engineer, and names the Junior or Sub Engineer (Distribution) as the officer responsible for scrutiny, the site visit and the proposal.
claims.notes: Designations tied to the decision, each with the step it owns in the published time-limit table.

claims.text: The K/West ward water works RTI manual publishes the office of the Assistant Engineer (Water Works) for that ward with its street address, telephone number with extension, e-mail address, office timings and visiting hours.
claims.notes: A contact route for the office that handles the application in that ward. Institutional contact details only; no individual officer's details are recorded here.

claims.text: The ward water works RTI manual states that on receipt of approval from the competent authority the applicant is informed by the issue of a Permission Form, which enlists various approvals and conditions, and that the permission form is issued by the Assistant Engineer Water Works of the ward.
claims.notes: A document the applicant receives after applying, naming what has been approved and on what conditions.

claims.text: The ward water works RTI manual's time limit table names preparation of a Permission Form or a rejection letter as a step, and signature of the permission form or rejection letter by the Assistant Engineer Water Works as the step after it.
claims.notes: A refusal reaches the applicant as a letter; the manual does not say whether the letter carries reasons.

claims.text: The ward water works RTI manual states that after compliance with the conditions of the permission form the water connection is released to the applicant.

The ward water works RTI manual states that complaints about water supply can be registered with the Complaint Officer of the respective ward office and also with the Water Control Office in the city.
claims.notes: A route for a supply complaint, not for the progress of a connection application.

claims.text: The corporation's New Water Connection route publishes only two application forms, for the slum category and for other categories, each last changed on 18 September 2015, and carries no guidance on eligibility, documents, charges, timelines or offices.
claims.notes: Direct current observation of the folder listing on the access date.

claims.text: Once a connection exists, the corporation's water citizen portal lets a consumer download a duplicate bill or a duplicate receipt by entering the consumer number, without login.
claims.notes: A surface that follows the connection, not the application; recorded for completeness and not used for the after-submission cell. The route was read only, with no consumer number entered. Basis boundary: the observation is of what the public page showed on the access date, duplicate bill and duplicate receipt options keyed to a consumer number and reachable without login; that a download is actually delivered is an inference from those published options, because confirming it would have required entering a real consumer number and querying live case data.

claims.text: Whether an applicant for a new water connection can check the progress of the application on any public route, and what reference number they are given when the papers are lodged, is not established by any reviewed public page.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related.

claims.text: What the citizen pays for the connection itself, beyond the Rs. 200 scrutiny fee, is not established by any reviewed public page: no deposit, connection charge, meter cost or road-opening charge figure is published on any route reviewed.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related; the charges manual is recorded as obtainable only from the PRO department on payment of fees.
